questions.prompt: With respect to lung volumes ...
options: The volume of gas left in the lungs after a maximal expiration is the functional residual volume
Vital capacity is the volume exhaled when a maximal inspiration is followed by a maximal expiration
FRC can be measured directly with a spirometer
Helium dilution measures the inspiratory capacity
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vital capacity is the maximal expiration following maximal inspiration. Residual volume remains after maximal expiration; FRC and other residual-containing volumes cannot be measured by simple spirometry.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 1; source page 1.

questions.prompt: In which zone of the lung is there the blood flow during both of systole and diastole?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In zone III, arterial and venous pressures exceed alveolar pressure throughout the cycle, allowing continuous flow during systole and diastole.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 2; source page 1.

questions.prompt: What is the chloride shift in RBC during CO2 transport?
options: Bicarbonate ion goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
Chloride ion goes into the cell and bicarbonate ion goes out of the cell
Chloride ion goes out of the cell and hydrogen ion goes into the cell
Hydrogen ion goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The usual chloride shift during systemic CO2 uptake exchanges bicarbonate exiting the erythrocyte for chloride entering. The exchange reverses in pulmonary capillaries during unloading.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 3; source page 1.

questions.prompt: With regard to the distribution of pulmonary blood flow, which one the following is correct?
options: The mean pulmonary arterial pressure is 15 mmHg
Blood flow is determined by the amount of alveolar ventilation
Typically there is a zone at the bottom that is not perfused
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The standard resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure is approximately 15 mmHg. Alveolar hypoxia constricts pulmonary vessels and the healthy dependent lung is well perfused.

questions.prompt: Which one the following factors causes that haemoglobin oxygen dissociation curve moves up and to the left?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Cooling increases hemoglobin oxygen affinity, shifting the dissociation curve left; exercise, acidosis and increased 2,3-DPG shift it right.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 5; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Regarding ventilation/perfusion differences in the lungs ...
options: V/Q ratio is high at the bottom
In healthy individuals, anatomical dead space is more than physiological dead space
The relative change in blood flow from apex to bottom is less than relative change in ventilation
V/Q differences are due to gravity
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Gravity contributes to the upright perfusion gradient; perfusion changes more than ventilation, so V/Q is higher at the apex. Physiological dead space cannot be smaller than its anatomical component.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 6; source page 2.

questions.prompt: How long does it take for blood to pass through the pulmonary capillaries when cardiac output is normal?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Normal resting pulmonary capillary transit is roughly 0.75–0.8 seconds; 0.8 seconds is the closest offered value. Exercise shortens transit while recruitment increases exchange capacity.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 7; source page 2.

questions.prompt: In control of ventilation, the medullary chemoreceptors respond to ...
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: H+ in brain extracellular fluid is the important direct stimulus. Blood CO2 crosses into brain fluids and generates H+, so CO2 is a major indirect stimulus rather than the requested direct chemical signal.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 8; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of vagal reflex on the respiratory system?
options: Increasing the cilia beating frequency in the mucosiliary system
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vagal cholinergic signaling contracts airway smooth muscle and promotes bronchoconstriction; beta-adrenergic signaling favors dilation.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 9; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about the role of the muscles in inspiration?
options: Relaxation of the abdominal recti lengthens the chest cavity and leads to expiration
Relaxation of diaphragm shortens the chest cavity and leads to expiration
Contraction of the scalene raises the rib cage and leads to expiration
Contraction of anterior serrati pulls the rib cage downward and leads to inspiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diaphragm relaxation reduces the vertical thoracic dimension and assists passive expiration. Although the stem says inspiration, this is the only correctly paired muscle action and phase among the choices.

questions.prompt: According to Laplace’s law, how does the collapse pressure change as the alveolar radius is reduced by half (surface tension is constant)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Laplace's relation P = 2T/r predicts double collapse pressure when radius is halved at fixed surface tension. The question number is at the end of page 2; its stem and options continue on page 3.

questions.prompt: With regard to the neural control of respiration ...
options: The dorsal respiratory group has expiratory neurons
The ventral respiratory group is located in the pons
The main respiratory control centre is located in the pons
Voluntary control system is located in the cerebral cortex
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Voluntary respiratory control originates in the cerebral cortex. Automatic rhythm and pattern depend on medullary and pontine networks, not a sole pontine center.

questions.prompt: If a patient's blood carries 12 grams of hemoglobin per deciliter, what is the O2 carrying capacity of his blood (milliliters per deciliter)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using 1.34 mL O2 per gram of fully saturated hemoglobin, 12 × 1.34 = 16.08 mL/dL, approximately 16. This excludes the small dissolved O2 component.

questions.prompt: Which one the following factors leads to physiological dead space?
options: Mixing pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
A decrease in cardiac output to half
A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
An increase in VA/Q ratio more than normal amount
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A high V/Q ratio directly describes wasted alveolar ventilation, but reduced cardiac output can also raise V/Q if ventilation is maintained. The broad causal wording does not make the supplied high-ratio answer uniquely exclusive.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 14; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Increase in which factor reduces the diffusion rate of oxygen?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increasing membrane thickness lengthens the diffusion path and reduces flux; greater area, solubility or pressure gradient would increase it.

evidence: Respiratory theory — 15 January 2022 (filename date); printed question 15; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about the ventral respiratory group (VRG) in the medulla?
options: Generates the inspiratory signal as a ramp signal
Its electrical stimulation only leads to an exhalation.
It has a fundamental role in respiratory basal rhythm
It has a role in increasing pulmonary ventilation during muscle activity and exercise.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The source selects increased ventilatory drive during exercise, which is true. However, ventral medullary networks including pre-Bötzinger neurons also have a fundamental rhythm-generating role, making the basal-rhythm choice defensible under modern physiology.

questions.prompt: What is the normal PO2 and PCO2 in the venous blood, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional mixed-venous reference gases are PO2 about 40 and PCO2 about 45 mmHg. The subscripts identify oxygen first and carbon dioxide second.

questions.prompt: compliance of the lung is reduced by all of the following except ...
options: By surgically removing part of the lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Emphysematous destruction reduces elastic recoil and increases compliance; fibrosis, edema and loss of lung tissue reduce total lung compliance.

questions.prompt: If the O2 diffusing capacity of a patient is 15 ml/min/mmHg, what will be the CO2 diffusing capacity (ml/min/mmHg)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the approximate CO2:O2 diffusion comparison of 20:1, 15 × 20 = 300 mL/min/mmHg. This is a textbook proportional estimate, not a universal exact measurement.

questions.prompt: Trachea is a part of ...
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The trachea is a conducting airway and contributes to anatomical dead space rather than the alveolar gas-exchange region.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is correct about Surfactant?
options: Surface tension is proportional to surfactant concentration
Is produced by type I alveolar cells
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant reduces surface tension and the inward/suction force that favors fluid entry, helping keep alveoli dry. It does not make surface tension zero and is produced by type II cells.
